messages:
From: Amira Bashir <amira.bashir@northbridge.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Vulnerability management questionnaire: follow-up + SBOM request

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the brief chat last week. Attached is Northbridge's standard vulnerability management questionnaire (PDF). We're evaluating several inference vendors and need to confirm a few details specifically around how you handle: SAST/DAST tooling and cadence, patch SLAs for CVE classes, pen test reports or summaries, and SBOM generation for hosted and dedicated deployments.

Could you please return a completed questionnaire or a point-by-point response by EOD Friday (2025-11-07)? Also:
- We're particularly interested in how you treat critical CVEs that affect third-party dependencies (e.g., CUDA runtime, MKL, libc) vs. model weights/serving-layer vulnerabilities.
- Do you provide a machine-readable SBOM and how often is it regenerated?
- Do you run external pen tests annually and can you share a redacted summary?

Attachments: Northbridge_VM_Questionnaire.pdf (12 pages)

Appreciate it — if useful we can schedule a short technical call.

Best,
Amira Bashir
Head of Vendor Security
Northbridge Financial
security@northbridge.com

--
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Amira Bashir <amira.bashir@northbridge.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, soojin.lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vulnerability management questionnaire: follow-up + SBOM request

Amira — thanks for sending this over. Attached are initial artifacts and a short cover note to speed review: Redwood_Security_Brief_Q42024.pdf (summary of controls & third-party assessments), redwood_sbom.tar.gz (machine-readable SBOM export for our hosted runtime, redacted PII), and a brief process doc (sast_dast_process.md).

High-level answers up front:
- SAST/DAST: We run continuous SAST across all service code and infra repos (federated Semgrep + Veracode for binary analysis) and weekly DAST scans of public-facing endpoints (OWASP ZAP + Burp on pre-prod). Critical results triaged within 24 hours.
- Patch SLAs: initial triage for Critical CVEs is 24 hours; mitigation plan within 7 days for hosted customers (mitigation can be configuration or patch); full security patch (hotfix or kernel/runtime update) targeted within 30 days depending on risk and vendor timelines. For Dedicated/Private deployments we offer accelerated remediation support in contracts (hotfix ETA can be contracted to 14 days).
- Pen tests: We run an external pen test annually by a third-party (Redwood Security Partners); we can provide a redacted executive summary.
- SBOM: Machine-readable SBOMs (CycloneDX JSON) are generated per release for the runtime images and published to the customer portal. For hosted infra we regenerate SBOMs each release (approx weekly); for Dedicated/Private we provide on-demand exports and can schedule monthly pushes to a secure bucket.

I'll follow up with the completed questionnaire in spreadsheet form by Friday and loop in Soojin for technical clarifications. If Northbridge needs specific SLA language we can add it to the MAP.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_Security_Brief_Q42024.pdf; redwood_sbom.tar.gz; sast_dast_process.md

--
From: Amira Bashir <amira.bashir@northbridge.com>

Subject: Re: Vulnerability management questionnaire: follow-up + SBOM request

Marcus — thank you, this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions so we can sign off with procurement: 

1) For 'mitigation within 7 days' — is that a hard SLA for critical vulnerabilities in the hosted offering, or an operational target? We need contractual language for Critical/High/MED classes.
2) For third-party runtime issues (e.g., CUDA, kernel CVEs), do you coordinate patching with cloud infra vendors or do you provide alternative mitigations (e.g., forced node rotation, runtime config disables)?
3) Can you confirm the redaction level for the pen test summary (we need at least asset-level descriptions and remediation status, but not PoC exploit code).
4) We'd like an explicit delivery date for the completed questionnaire and a recommended MAP with milestones and owners.

Procurement is also asking for a sample security addendum clause for patch SLA — can you provide language we can circulate internally?

If it's easier, let's do a 30-minute call Friday at 10am ET.

Regards,
Amira

--
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Amira Bashir <amira.bashir@northbridge.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Vulnerability management questionnaire: follow-up + SBOM request

Amira — thanks for the great questions. I'm Soojin (Director, Security Engineering) and Marcus looped me in to provide the technical detail. Below are concrete answers and proposed contractual language that should map cleanly into a security addendum.

1) SLA definitions (proposed)
- Critical (CVE score >=9.0 or active exploit targeting production): initial triage within 24 hours, mitigation strategy within 72 hours (temporary mitigation acceptable), remediation deployment (hotfix or vendor patch) within 30 days for hosted customers.
- High (7.0–8.9): initial triage within 48 hours, mitigation within 7 days, remediation within 60 days.
- Medium (4.0–6.9): triage within 7 days, remediation windows aligned to regular release cadence (30–90 days).

Notes on scope: SLAs above apply to Redwood-managed hosted clusters and managed customer tenants. For Dedicated and Private deployments, Redwood will provide incident response support and backport/delivery ETA commitments; customers may elect an accelerated SLA (contractually agreed, e.g., Critical remediation within 14 days) as a paid add-on.

2) Third-party runtime CVEs
- For infra-level (CUDA, glibc, kernel), Redwood maintains a supplier-tracking log. We coordinate with cloud infra partners for patch scheduling where kernel-level patches are needed; when coordination is not immediate we provide compensating controls (node isolation, forced node drain/rotation, updated container images pinned to patched base images) and publish recommended mitigation steps in the customer portal.

3) Pen test summaries
- We will provide a redacted executive summary that includes: scope, methodology, assets tested (high level), discovered issues by severity, remediation status per issue, and verification notes. We redact exploit PoC and any customer-identifying data. Expected delivery: 7 business days after request for the latest engagement summary.

4) SBOM cadence and format
- SBOM format: CycloneDX JSON (component + dependency graph).
- Hosted: SBOM regenerated per runtime image release (typical cadence: weekly).
- Dedicated/Private: SBOM export available on demand; can be scheduled monthly or triggered by a security event. We can push to a mutually-owned S3/GCS bucket or provide via secure portal.

5) Tooling and verification
- SAST: Semgrep (ruleset + PR gating) + Veracode for packaged artifacts.
- DAST: OWASP ZAP baseline + authenticated Burp scans for customer-facing endpoints in pre-prod.
- Dependency scanning: Snyk with automated open-source dependency alerts and ticketing.
- Fuzzing & model-surface checks: internal fuzz harness (SigMA) for runtime APIs and continuous differential tests on model inputs.

6) Proposed MAP (milestones & owners)
- 2025-11-07: Redwood returns completed questionnaire (owner: Marcus Lin) — DONE (spreadsheet attached to MAP).
- 2025-11-10: Deliver redacted pen test executive summary (owner: Soojin Lee).
- 2025-11-12: Legal/procurement review of proposed SLA language and security addendum (owner: Laura Bennett).
- 2025-11-18: Finalize MAP and sign security addendum (owners: Redwood Legal + Northbridge Procurement).

7) Sample clause for security addendum (suggested language)
"Redwood shall maintain vulnerability management and remediation processes as described in the Vendor Security Brief. For Critical vulnerabilities affecting Redwood-managed services, Redwood shall: (a) commence triage within 24 hours of identification; (b) implement a mitigation strategy within 72 hours; (c) deploy a remediation or hotfix within 30 days, except where remediation is dependent on third-party vendor patches, in which case Redwood will provide compensating controls and a documented mitigation plan." 

Artifacts & attachments: completed questionnaire (spreadsheet) uploaded to the Drive link below; pen test summary will be delivered as a redacted PDF.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwoodSecurity

If you'd like the 10am ET slot today, Marcus can join and we can go line-by-line.

—
Soojin Lee

Redwood Inference
